question: According to the October 2025 Monetary Policy Report of the Reserve Bank of India, the revised GDP growth forecast for India for FY 2025–26 is _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**6.8%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Monetary Policy Report** released by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **October 2025**, the revised **GDP growth forecast** for India for the **Financial Year 2025–26** has been projected at **6.8%**.
 
• The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, which is responsible for fixing the benchmark interest rates in India, revised these growth estimates based on a comprehensive assessment of the **macroeconomic outlook** and **global economic trends**.
 
• The **real GDP growth** projection of **6.8%** reflects the resilience of the **Indian economy**, driven by robust **domestic demand**, improving **private investment**, and sustained **government capital expenditure**.
 
• The report indicates that the **services sector** and **manufacturing activity** remain the primary engines of growth, while the **agricultural sector** is expected to benefit from favorable **monsoon conditions** in the preceding year.
 
• The **RBI** utilizes sophisticated **economic modeling** and **high-frequency indicators** to arrive at these projections, ensuring that the monetary policy stance remains aligned with the objective of maintaining **price stability** while supporting growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):** 
 
 
• Established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, it serves as India's **central bank** and regulatory body for the banking system.
 
• Its primary functions include the **issuance of currency**, managing **foreign exchange reserves**, and acting as a **banker to the government** and other banks.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):** 
 
 
• The **MPC** is a **six-member committee** constituted by the **Central Government** under **Section 45ZB** of the amended **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• It is chaired by the **Governor of the RBI** and meets at least **four times a year** to decide on the **policy repo rate** required to achieve the **inflation target**.
 
 
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP):** 
 
 
• **GDP** is the total **monetary or market value** of all the finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period, typically a **financial year**.
 
• In India, the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, is responsible for calculating and releasing GDP data.
 
 
 
• **Financial Year in India:** 
 
 
• The **Financial Year (FY)** in India begins on **April 1** and ends on **March 31** of the following calendar year. Therefore, **FY 2025–26** covers the period from **April 2025 to March 2026**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **October 2025 report** factors in several **global risks**, including **geopolitical tensions**, **volatility in global commodity prices**, and the **monetary policy actions** of major central banks like the **US Federal Reserve**.
 
• The **output gap**—the difference between **actual output** and **potential output**—is a key metric monitored by the **RBI** to determine if the economy is operating at full capacity without generating excessive **inflation**.
 
• The **6.8% growth** target is supported by a significant increase in **bank credit growth** and healthy **corporate balance sheets**, which encourage fresh **capacity expansion** (Capex) by the private sector.
 
• **Inflation targeting** remains a core focus of the RBI, with a medium-term target of **4%** within a band of **+/- 2%**, as per the **flexible inflation targeting framework** adopted in **2016**.
